status: Proposed technical/readiness work; no new owner decisions

gaps.topic: Exact native worker and link identity
gaps.gap: No linked isolated worker/final linker recipe or image-dependency record exists. libsqlite3.a contains SQLCipher; a system -lsqlite3/wrapper substitution would invalidate qualification.
gaps.resolve: Specify exact retained archive/header, entry point, initialization hooks and link closure; review image/symbol/version probes before separately authorized adapter construction.

gaps.topic: Owned key/scope/handle lifecycle and failure contract
gaps.gap: The compile-only helper accepts a bare sqlite3 pointer and 32-byte buffer; it does not open/authenticate/identify stores, enforce native scope/epoch, own close/cursors or define consumed-vs-borrowed input on every rejection path. Early invalid-input return does not wipe that buffer itself.
gaps.resolve: Define exact native ownership/lease protocol, open-existing/create split, key-before-access sequence, authenticated identity gate, typed coarse error mapping, real close barrier and scratch/provider cleanup semantics. No raw key in Domain/Ports/Core/UI.

gaps.gap: WAL/FULL/foreign keys/memory-temp and cipher suite are defined, but exact settings order, macOS fullfsync/checkpoint_fullfsync, memory-security activation and finite busy/deadline settings are not frozen. The pinned memory-security getter also depends on allocator activity; the switch is process-global enable-only.
gaps.resolve: Record a reviewed setting/order/readback table per normal-WAL and rollback-diagnostic worker. Recommend memory security ON in a fresh worker; do not silently promote this recommendation to the existing contract. Reject missing required getter results, not just nonzero setter errors.

gaps.gap: Positive main/WAL plaintext controls exist, but no instrumented encrypted artifact or transient/unlinked I/O coverage exists. Directory scans alone miss short-lived/unlinked writes; SHM metadata cannot be called encrypted.
gaps.resolve: Review a bounded native I/O/VFS observation design covering named and unnamed files, operation phases and encryption boundaries, with functioning public-marker controls and cleanup traces. Do not capture key bytes or raw sensitive buffers.

gaps.topic: Synthetic database identity and expected-state ledger
gaps.gap: No reviewed implemented schema/fixture defines exact scope, suite, schema/key generation, revision, receipts, row corpus and malformed/tamper offsets for the planned worker.
gaps.resolve: Freeze test-only schema/version, full expected records, scope mismatch controls, source-audited mutation offsets and typed result/error oracles; preserve canonical product schema decisions.

gaps.topic: Failure injection, cancellation and terminal outcomes
gaps.gap: No barrier-driven supervisor, VFS error injection or mutation/receipt/promotion checkpoints exist. Random sleeps/kills and unspecified error states cannot establish recovery.
gaps.resolve: Specify exact before/after commit/checkpoint/write/promotion hooks, PID/start-token ownership, emitted durable/acknowledged ledger states, bounded fault ordinals and per-cutpoint acceptable outcomes. Ambiguity prevents a PASS.

gaps.gap: The contract selects quiesced encrypted copy-and-promote rather than in-place rekey, but no exact public copy API, protected destination setup or durable intent/promotion protocol is frozen.
gaps.resolve: Specify and review a public provider-supported copy mechanism and its encrypted output, identity/key-generation checks, retained old branch and promotion checkpoints. Multi-resource backups, custody and second-Mac recovery remain EXP-04/07 work.

gaps.topic: Owned environment, secrets channel and safe cleanup
gaps.gap: Current compiler/SDK and static inputs exist, but the runtime run root/process/resource manifest, secret-only memory/channel ownership, stop policy and cleanup protocol have not been exercised.
gaps.resolve: Review per-case owned paths/processes, exclusive scope, finite resource guards, no core dumps/key logs, failure retention and quiescent cleanup. No personal stores, real Keychain, WebKit/native prompts or host-disk exhaustion.
